headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Firecrawl can egress broadly and handle API keys, while LlamaFactory has no network or filesystem access, limiting the pair mostly to prompt-injection and workflow errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl can ingest web content and expose it through MCP-compatible/API workflows, so malicious content could be copied into LlamaFactory as instructions if an operator bridges them manually. LlamaFactory has no clipboard, files, or MCP surfaces, so the pathway is not automatic and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies Firecrawl output into LlamaFactory prompts without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF Firecrawl content is treated as instructions rather than data, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Paste only extracted data, not raw HTML or markdown.
Add a fixed instruction prefix that tells LlamaFactory to ignore embedded directives.
Review Firecrawl outputs for prompt-like text before reuse.
Use a separate human verification step before any downstream action.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys and has broad network egress, so it can transmit sensitive material outward. LlamaFactory has no network egress and no filesystem or API surfaces, so it is not the exfiltration side; the pair risk comes from Firecrawl handling sensitive inputs in a default online workflow.
conditions: IF Firecrawl is pointed at pages containing secrets or API keys, those values can leave the local environment.
IF the operator routes Firecrawl outputs into external services, sensitive content may be duplicated.
mitigations: Restrict Firecrawl targets to non-sensitive domains.
Redact API keys before crawling or scraping.
Disable or avoid any downstream export of raw outputs.
Run a quick content scan for secrets before sharing results.
Use separate credentials for crawling and analysis.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl has broad network egress and supports multiple instances, but LlamaFactory has no filesystem write, no git modification, no shell, and no network egress. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface in the profiles, so a direct capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is later given write or network capabilities outside this profile, conflict risk could emerge.
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory in read-only analysis mode.
Avoid mounting shared writable directories.
Do not grant git or shell permissions to LlamaFactory.
Document any future shared resource before enabling it.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl can produce scraped facts and structured data, and LlamaFactory can be used to generate downstream model outputs from those inputs. Because LlamaFactory has no built-in verification or external grounding shown here, Firecrawl errors or hallucinated extractions could cascade into incorrect support responses or decisions.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is used as authoritative input to LlamaFactory prompts, errors can propagate.
IF no human verification step exists between extraction and response generation, cascading mistakes are likely.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before reuse of Firecrawl outputs.
Require citations or source URLs in downstream prompts.
Compare extracted facts against the original page for a sample of items.
Flag low-confidence extractions for manual checking.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl handles web content and API keys and may process regulated or personal data, while LlamaFactory shows no data classes touched and no network or filesystem access. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so the compliance concern is limited to operator-controlled handling of sensitive web data in Firecrawl.
conditions: IF Firecrawl processes personal data subject to retention or residency rules, compliance obligations apply.
IF outputs are stored or forwarded outside approved systems, policy violations can occur.
mitigations: Avoid crawling regulated content unless approved.
Minimize retention of raw crawl artifacts.
Strip secrets from logs and exports.
Confirm data handling policy before processing sensitive sites.
